summary.title: Array Indexing Diagram
summary.summary: The visual diagram shows zero‑based indexing of a 5‑element array and its relation to the length property. The audio narration discussed assigning arr[2] = 99 to update the third element, the fact that arrays are mutable and that the array reference stays the same, that arr.length is a read‑only field used as a loop bound, and that new arrays are initialized with default values (0 for numeric, false for boolean, null for object).
key_concepts: Elements are numbered starting at index 0
Last valid index equals length minus 1
numbers.length reports the total element count
arr[2] = 99; updates the third element
Arrays are mutable containers
The array reference itself stays the same
arr.length gives the array size
length is a field, not a method (no parentheses)
Commonly used as a loop bound
Numeric arrays default to 0
Boolean arrays default to false
Object reference arrays default to null
summary.voiceover_script: Zero‑based indexing is illustrated across a 5‑element array, showing indexes 0‑4 and the length property equal to 5. Assigning a new value, e.g., arr[2] = 99, updates the third element while the array reference stays the same. The length field is a read‑only field, not a method, often used as a loop bound. Newly created arrays receive default values: 0 for numerics, false for booleans, null for object references.

summary.summary: Example runtime error triggered by accessing an array index equal to its length.
key_concepts: Valid indices for a length-5 array are 0 through 4
arr[5] is out of bounds and throws an exception
The error occurs at runtime, not compile time
Arrays.sort(arr) sorts the array in place

Arrays.binarySearch(arr, key) requires a pre-sorted array
summary.code_example:

summary.voiceover_script: The java.util.Arrays class provides static helper methods such as sort, toString, and binarySearch. These methods are useful for array manipulation. The runtime error shown in this slide is a classic ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException, caused by accessing index 5 on a length-5 array.

summary.title: Arrays Utility Class and Arrays vs ArrayList
summary.summary: According to the instructor, the Arrays utility class includes common methods such as Arrays.sort, Arrays.toString, and Arrays.binarySearch. Arrays are fixed-size and store primitives directly, while ArrayList is resizable and part of the Collections framework. The choice between them depends on whether the collection size needs to change during program execution.
